(1) We propose a simple approach to improve machine interpret-ability of processed images, and show that it can transfer to other recognition tasks, architectures and datasets; and (2) We try to explain the transferability phenomenon by analyzing the similarities of different recognition models' decision boundaries.

we propose a simple method to enhance recognition quality of processed images and that it has strong transferability to different recognition tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem that the images optimized for human perception may not be recognized accurately by machines, which is a critical problem for the deployment of vision applications at a large scale.
the following questions: 1. How to make processed images better recognized by machines? 2. Can the recognition-aware processing models transfer to different architectures and datasets?
the following question: can we design image processing algorithms that improve machine interpretability? We believe that the answer is affirmative.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transferability of the recognition-aware image processing is a result of the similarity in the decision boundaries of different models.
the transferability of the proposed methods can be explained by the similarities of decision boundaries between different models.
our work provides a simple yet powerful approach for improving machine interpretability of images, with strong transferability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methods can help to improve the recognition quality of processed images, which may benefit the downstream applications of vision systems.
we propose a new paradigm for image processing, which aims to optimize the image quality for both human perception and machine recognition, with a focus on the latter.
the image processing methods can be optimized for better recognition quality, with the resulting improvement being transferable across recognition models and tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
image processing methods should be designed not only for humans, but also for machines.
the image processing community should consider the machine interpretability of images as a design goal, in addition to human perception.
the image processing network can be designed to be recognition-aware, and the resulting images are more interpretable by future recognition models, even if the recognition model is unknown.
